title: Schoolhouse Slate — Chalk & Numeral Lesson
description: A chalkboard-faithful slide for elementary math lessons: slate-green ground with visible dust texture, rough chalk-stroke numerals, a hand-drawn date frame at the top, and a corner apple doodle — every mark looks like it was drawn with real chalk.
philosophy: This template exists because children learn better in environments that feel familiar and human, not sleek and corporate. It rejects smooth system fonts, pixel-perfect geometry, and any finish that reads as 'software.' Every stroke must carry visible hand-pressure, as if lifted directly from a classroom board. It is built for teachers who want their slides to be an extension of the physical room, not an escape from it.
goodFor: Elementary-school arithmetic and step-by-step problem walkthroughs
Back-to-school night or parent-teacher event slides
Educational video thumbnails and lesson-intro title cards
Homeschool curriculum printables adapted to screen
avoidFor: Chart-heavy data dashboards requiring precise axis labels
Investor pitch decks or corporate quarterly reviews
Any context where rough chalk edges read as unfinished or unprofessional
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a teacher just finished writing on a real chalkboard — chalk dust settling, strokes of uneven pressure visible in every mark. Compositionally asymmetric: the date frame and apple doodle act as warm counterweights to the centered title, creating lively but unforced balance. The mood is nostalgic and inviting, evoking a sunlit classroom rather than a digital surface. Avoid any finish that reads as designed — no clean edges, no uniform stroke weight, no modern minimalism.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed slate-ground canvas with no margin bands — texture and chalk dust live edge-to-edge. A hand-drawn rectangular date frame is anchored in the upper-left quadrant, occupying roughly the top 18% of slide height and left 35% of width. The main title sits centered horizontally across the vertical midpoint of the board, underscored by a single wavy chalk rule line; the subtitle follows immediately below at a narrower span. A corner apple doodle is fixed to the lower-right, roughly 10% inset from each edge, serving as a decorative closing flourish with no page number on this slide.

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a mid-lesson chalkboard — purposeful and pedagogical but unmistakably human-made. Composition is asymmetric: large chalk step-numerals create a strong left anchor while worked problem text and small inline diagrams breathe across the open right field. Every element — underlines, separator rules, connecting arrows — reads as drawn with real chalk, varying in pressure and slight wobble. Avoid anything typeset, symmetric, or digitally smooth; the organized messiness is precisely the warmth.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with an 8% outer margin on all sides. A chalk-underlined topic heading occupies the top strip spanning cols 2–11; below it, two to three vertically stacked step-blocks each place a large rough step-numeral in the left gutter (cols 1–2) with problem content and small worked diagrams filling cols 3–11. Hand-drawn ruled lines divide each block from the next. A corner apple doodle anchors the bottom-right, and a faint page marker sits bottom-center.
